question.worked_solution:
First, we decompose all of the terms into their various factors. The $12(x-1)$ in the numerator becomes $2\cdot 2\cdot 3\cdot (x-1),$ and the $15x$ in the denominator becomes $3\cdot 5\cdot x.$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{12(x-1)}{15x}=\frac{2\cdot 2\cdot 3\cdot (x-1)}{3\cdot 5\cdot x}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we cancel out all the pairs of common factors in the numerator and denominator. In this case, there is one pair of $3$'s.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2\cdot 2\cdot 3\cdot (x-1)}{3\cdot 5\cdot x} & = \\ \frac{2\cdot 2\cdot \cancel{3}\cdot (x-1)}{\cancel{3}\cdot 5\cdot x} & = \\ \frac{2\cdot 2\cdot (x-1)}{5\cdot x} & = \\ \frac{4(x-1)}{5x}\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the expression simplifies to $\frac{4(x-1)}{5x}.$
